data.title: Chlorpheniramine maleate
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antihistamines_

**Class:** First-generation (sedating) H1 antihistamine — alkylamine

## Mechanism of action
- H1 inverse agonist; crosses blood–brain barrier; anticholinergic

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acute urticaria, allergic reactions, itch, insect bites; adjunct (IV/IM) in anaphylaxis

## Dose & formulations
- Adults 4 mg every 4–6 h (max 24 mg/day); injection 10 mg IM/IV; children 0.35 mg/kg/day

## Adverse effects
- Sedation (milder than other first-generation drugs), anticholinergic effects, paradoxical excitation in children

## Contraindications
- Neonates; caution in glaucoma, prostatism, epilepsy

## Drug interactions
- Alcohol and CNS depressants; MAO inhibitors; phenytoin levels may rise

## Pregnancy & lactation
Widely used in pregnancy (long safety record).

## Viva points
- Alkylamine — least sedating first-generation antihistamine; long pregnancy safety record

_Sources: Khopkar (First generation H1 antihistamines); Wolverton 4e ch.32. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
